Capability.meaning: Explicit operation grant on a resource or permission scope.

PrincipalGroup.meaning: Direct membership in a configured role or user group; a group can itself be a member. Supplied by trusted configuration or an authoritative identity source, never inferred from an agent-chosen name.

ResourceGroup.meaning: Permission-scope membership; grants on a parent apply to its descendants.

InGroup.meaning: Direct or nested role/user-group membership from PrincipalGroup. Membership alone is not permission.

Can.meaning: Grant including declared principal and resource memberships; not final authorization.

Field.meaning: Host-observed field or association of an application object or event. The binding defines cardinality, value type, fixed unit and optional observation-time field; never agent claims or hidden policy decisions.

Event.meaning: An event observed by the host, with its ID, actor and kind; recording it does not imply permission or success.

scope: Captured gate inputs and mediated callbacks. Outcomes follow the trusted adapter's confirmation contract; they are not independent proof of business success or authentic identity. Unmediated channels and missing observations remain outside this trace.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Name the horizon for both multiples, put them on one basis, source the index to S&P Dow Jones Indices or a primary feed, and add Apple's FY2026-basis multiple so the premium is not understated by a two-year-forward EPS.","evidence_request":"What are Apple's and the S&P 500's forward P/E on a stated next-twelve-month basis at 2026-10-30, and what is Apple's consensus FY2026 EPS?","issue":"The 35.2x forward against 18.09x for the index carries the premium argument in five sections, but rests on two aggregators (S97 FinanceCharts, S146 Trendonify) and neither states a horizon. Apple's is on $9.79, which the report calls FY2027 EPS; the index figure is normally next-twelve-month. On FY2026 EPS of $8.90 the same price is 38.7x.","sections":["executive_summary","funding_valuation","scoring"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Either use a primary consensus (U7 is already open) and give the median, analyst count and date, or downgrade to 'aggregator estimates of $338-355' labelled unverified and stop calling it the sell side's median.","evidence_request":"What is the median twelve-month price target and analyst count as of 2026-10-30 from a primary consensus source?","issue":"'The sell side's median target of $338-355' is a range presented as a median, drawn from two low-confidence scrapers (S142, S144), and it carries the non-consensus claim that the Street sees fair value here and that 'there is no analyst catalyst'. That is too load-bearing a conclusion for low-confidence aggregator data.","sections":["executive_summary","thesis","scoring"],"severity":"Important"},{"action":"Re-cite the 65% share to S94 and call it a Counterpoint estimate of premium-unit share in H1 2026; label the modem and Duo specifications as reported and unverified; mark the ecosystem figure as company-stated.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Claims stated as fact on the wrong or a company source: the 65% premium-phone share is cited to filings (S5 in section 5; S6, S113 in section 14) though it is Counterpoint's estimate (S94); the in-house C2 modem is fact in section 14 but 'reported' in section 3 (S112); the Duo rests on TechCrunch (S114) and the $149bn ecosystem on Apple's own claim, with no status label.","sections":["competition","scoring","technology_product"],"severity":"Important"}]
parameters.notes: Checked every material claim's source, date and independence. The primary-filing spine is clean: S1-S6 cover FY2021-FY2025 and the June 2026 10-Q, peer comparisons rest on S13, S49, S50, S103, S105, S107, S109, and the market data are uniformly timestamped 2026-10-31. Company-only claims are mostly labelled as required - the 2.5bn installed base is called an earnings-call figure, the Gemini licence 'reported' and unconfirmed, the $20bn search payment a litigated estimate. Dated sources are used where they matter: the 2022 payment is dated, the 2025-12-05 judgment and 2025-12-11 Ninth Circuit opinion are dated, and no claim rests on a source older than 2025 except the FY2021 10-K and the Cisco precedent. Two dated items are mixed without a basis label: the search payment is quoted as 16.6% of TTM services revenue and 18.3% of FY2025, both correctly computed, but the executive briefing and section 14 use the FY2025 basis only. The Red Team's own company-only inventory (five claims) matches what I found, and each is labelled in its section.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Add rows for OPPO, vivo and Honor (premium share and ASP), Transsion (India and emerging markets), Microsoft Copilot and OpenAI as assistant substitutes that could disintermediate the Siri layer, and the certified-refurbished channel as a unit substitute, each with share, price band and source; state which are immaterial and why.","evidence_request":"What are OPPO, vivo and Honor's shares of the $600-plus China segment in 2026, and what evidence is there that ChatGPT or Copilot usage displaces Siri on iOS?","issue":"Section 5's competitor table omits four rival sets the report references elsewhere: OPPO, vivo and Honor in China premium (section 4 lists them and the top six hold 96% of China), Transsion in India and Africa, Microsoft and OpenAI for the assistant layer (the Gemini licence is treated as a supplier risk, never as a substitute that could take the assistant off iOS), and refurbished units.","sections":["competition"],"severity":"Important"}]
parameters.notes: Rethinking the peer set against the four challenges. Geographic: the table covers the US, China and Korea and omits the Chinese mid-premium trio that section 4 itself names - OPPO, vivo and Honor - and Transsion, the volume leader in India and Africa where the report says emerging markets fall more than 20% in 2026. Adjacent giants: Microsoft and OpenAI are the real adjacent entrants for the assistant layer. Apple has licensed Gemini and rents TPUs, so the layer that sells the handset is supplied by a competitor; a Copilot or ChatGPT default that reaches iPhone users changes what Apple sells, and the xAI suit noted in section 10 is the only trace of this threat. The report's strongest strategic point - that the AI race may not be the thing that sells phones - argues against OpenAI being immaterial, so it needs explicit treatment or explicit dismissal. Substitute: the refurbished and used market is a direct unit substitute in a market whose units fall 16.7% while ASPs rise 27.6%, and it is absent. Open source: on-device open models that can serve as assistants are implied by the rented frontier in section 3 but not assessed. Academic: not applicable beyond Apple's own arXiv reports, which are cited. Samsung is correctly the volume rival and Huawei the profit rival; both are well evidenced.

parameters.items: [{"action":"Quantify the demand mechanism: replacement cycle or upgrade rate from IDC or Counterpoint, the channel (carrier instalments, Apple Upgrade leasing), and the observed response to the $100 iPhone 18 Pro rise, and name the unit or mix disclosure that would settle it.","evidence_request":"What is the current average smartphone replacement cycle and Apple's upgrade rate, and what sell-through evidence followed the $100 price rise?","issue":"The budget owner, annual September cycle and China switcher evidence are covered, but 'price-led growth is the most reversible kind' and the base case's 9%-to-5% fade rest on no upgrade rate, replacement-cycle length or elasticity estimate, and there is no lost-deal or churn evidence anywhere - the weakest link in the demand case.","sections":["business_model","market"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"Use one probability distribution in both sections; reconcile the over-60% margin-below-46% probability with the 50% base weight or re-weight; fix the bear at one number and one EPS year; label every multiple-based value with its EPS year and state the EPS year behind the FY2029 IRR.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Section 10 puts the chance of hardware gross margin below 46% - a case it values at $270 - at 'over 60%', yet section 11's 50% base underwrites 47-48% and $284 and its 25% bull holds 48%. The bear is $242 in section 10, $241 in section 11 and $214 at 24.6x on trailing EPS; the 31.0x mean gives $270 on trailing EPS (section 10) and $303 on FY2027 EPS (section 8).","sections":["risk","thesis","scoring"],"severity":"Critical"},{"action":"State each figure with its metric, base period and basket (contract or spot, DRAM or NAND, year on year or against the 2025 average), show the cost increase implied by the 47-48% margin and the 46% break-point, and use one figure throughout.","evidence_request":"What is the 2026 DRAM and NAND contract-price increase on a like-for-like year-on-year basis, and what share of the iPhone 18 Pro bill of materials is memory at each point?","issue":"Memory cost is quantified two ways with no bridge: sections 7 and 10 say prices rose 146% in Q1 2026 against the 2025 average (S68, which reports Samsung's memory ASP), while sections 4 and 5 say NAND and DRAM are more than 300% above a year earlier (IDC, S84). The base case's 47-48% margin and the 46% break-point rest on which is right.","sections":["financials","risk","market","competition"],"severity":"Critical"},{"action":"Reproduce the calculation or drop the number; if it uses a fat-tail loss, show it, since the stated three-outcome spread implies a fraction above 100%.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Full Kelly at $270 of 39% is not reproducible: on the stated returns from $270 (+32%, +5%, -11%) the optimum exceeds 100% of the fund; adding the $133 tail makes it negative. The 3.9% used is unexplained.","sections":["scoring"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"Recompute both: from $344.63 a 34x exit on FY2029 EPS of $11.45 gives 4.5% a year, and 9% needs about 39x; at $270, 31x gives 9.9%. The grid implies 9-16% per 50bp, not 15-18%.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Two sensitivity claims fail against the report's own arithmetic: 'a 34x exit is needed for a three-year IRR near 9%' from $344.63, and 'each 50bp on the rate moves value by 15-18%' - the section 8 grid gives 9-16% per 50bp depending on where on the curve.","sections":["thesis","funding_valuation","risk"],"severity":"Minor"},{"action":"Reconcile to one FY2025 buyback figure and one market capitalisation, and label each services margin with its period.","evidence_request":"","issue":"Small internal variances: FY2025 buybacks are $90.7bn in sections 1 and 8 but $89.3bn in section 9; market capitalisation is $5,029.6bn in most sections but $5,072bn in sections 6 and 7; services gross margin appears as 75.4%, 76.0% and 76.3% without period labels.","sections":["strategy","business_model","financials","funding_valuation"],"severity":"Minor"}]
parameters.notes: Stress arithmetic that reproduces: probability-weighted value $291.5 = 0.25x357 + 0.5x284 + 0.25x241, -15.4% from $344.63; weighted composite 6.05 on the stated weights; sum of the parts $177.4 = (23x62.7 + 12x92.1 + 62.2)/14.715; the three-year IRR grid at $344.63, $300, $270 and $240 with FY2029 EPS $11.45, $3.55 of dividends and 27x/31x/34x reproduces to the decimal; 200bp of gross margin = $0.52 of EPS (6.0%) and the $20bn payment = $1.12 (12.9%); buyback yields 1.63% gross and 1.36% net; the DCF grid interpolates to $212 at 9.0%/4.0%. Thirty per cent worse on the key numbers: FY2027 EPS $6.85 at 29x is $199, so the $270 entry would need 39x - the entry price does not survive a 30% EPS miss, but the recommendation does, because the position is zero and the franchise survives: revenue 30% lower still leaves net cash and stops the buyback before the balance sheet. A 30% lower normalised FCF is $87.6bn, 57.4x, which covers the $82.2bn buyback but not $97.9bn of buybacks and dividends. A 30% worse memory cost than the 46% case takes fair value into the low $240s, which is the bear - so the bear is the right downside anchor and the $133 DCF is not. The three facts I would most want before a real decision are the 2 November margin guide, the FY2026 10-K other-liabilities note and the D.C. Circuit schedule.
